The prior source identifies melan- + -oma; Etymonline links the word to melano-. These are analyses of an overlap, not independent proof that the same o is two segmental morphemes. Retain melano as a same-family lookup alias for the verified black component; no claim that the full melano- combining form was independently concatenated to -oma.

The dictionary-supported melano lookup is a variant relationship, not a claim that its o is independently assigned to the first element in every historical analysis.
Sandal is independently productive English noun and verb (sandaled, sandaling). This source example can refer to the open shoe; do not conflate with sandal meaning sandalwood.

Sandal shoe and historical sandal fragrant wood are etymologically distinct. Sandaled is footwear, while sandalwood uses the separate fragrant-wood word; sandallike and sandalwood independently establish their respective bases.

arrogance 经 arrogantia、arrogare 源自 rogare ask；既有 rog / ask 目标已包含该词，两来源 scope 可对应同一目标。
arrogant 来自拉丁 arrogans，arrogare 由 ad- 与 rogare ask 构成；语义为历史引申，四个来源同归已发布 rog / ask。
arrogate 来自 arrogatus，arrogare 由 ad- 与 rogare ask 构成；两个来源同归已发布 rog / ask。
derogate 源自 derogare，de- 加 rogare 问或提议；两来源适用现有 rog / ask，语义属历史引申。
derogatory 经拉丁 derogatus 源于 de- 加 rogare 问、提议；两来源适配现有 rog / ask，词义为历史引申。
interrogate 经 interrogare 含 rogare 问，两个来源对应现有 rog / ask，词条已存在；这是来源范围核实。
interrogation 和 interrogate 经拉丁 interrogare（含 rogare 问），interrogat- 是过去分词词干；匹配已出版 ask 目标，此为历史词干索引。
Latin interrogare question contains inter- plus rogare; interrogat- is its past-participial stem and historical lookup alias.
prerogative 经拉丁 praerogativus 原指先被问及，来自 rogare 问；rogat 为历史词干索引，来源符合现有 ask 目标。
rogation 经拉丁 rogatio 源自 rogare 的过去分词词干，含询问、请求义；与已出版 rog “ask” 目标相符，不主张现代分词边界。

Latin rogare ask/propose underlies abrogate, derogation, arrogant and surrogacy/surrogate via prefixed legal verbs; actual modern meanings include repeal, detract or substitute, not necessarily asking. Preserve all historical accepts and each source scope. Take away in a source reflects prefixed derivative semantics, not an independent basic meaning of rog-.
